messages:
alex: quick proposal — run a probabilistic region-steering mode for Premium customers + model-variant hedging. goal: keep p99 latency stable while using cheaper regions as long as they meet probes.

maya: short version: pick region A with 80% / region B 20% by default, run continuous probes, if region A probe fails degrade to B but keep some hedged traffic to detect recovery.

ryan: how does this play with reserved capacity for Dedicated vs Hosted? we need to avoid hitting shared capacity quotas unintentionally.

alex: good point. plan is: tier-aware weight caps. config would look like:```json
{"steering_policy": "probabilistic", "weights": {"us-west": 0.8, "eu-central": 0.2}, "tier_caps": {"premium": {"min_reserve": 0.6}}, "fallback": {"type": "variant", "variants": ["gptx-8b-q8", "gptx-8b-q4_0"]}, "probe": {"interval_s": 10, "timeout_ms": 250} }```

erin: I like the variant fallback piece — if a region is healthy but CPU/GPU is hot, we can route to a quantized variant with slightly different latency/quality and log quality regressions. need to add eval hooks.

sam: telemetry/alerts: we should emit these signals: region_probe_latency, region_probe_fail_rate, steering_decision, variant_fallback_count, tier_capacity_usage. dashboards for each customer (or tenant) and aggregate.

maya: UX/console thought: rollout slider should support "probabilistic by region" with a per-region weight input, plus a checkbox for "hedge X% during degradations". show expected cost delta inline.

console-product: +1 on cost delta visibility. also need an override button ("force local region") for SREs and tenant admins. and a clear audit log entry when fallback happens.

ryan: internal API discussion: do we keep routing policy as an inline field on the route resource, or a separate steering_policy resource referenced by multiple routes? separate resource makes reuse easier across routes and simplifies rollout. downside: more entities to manage in console.

alex: leaning towards separate steering_policy resource. can version it and support canary attach. Example flow: create steering_policy v1 -> attach to routes -> canary 5% -> increase.

deploy-bot: canary started for steering_policy:policy-347 v1 -> attached to route:customers/premium -> 5% traffic in eu-central for 30m :rocket:

erin: ops checklist before broad rollout: 1) dashboard with per-region p50/p95/p99 for requests + probes 2) alerts for probe_fail_rate > 1% for 10m 3) cost anomaly monitor for tiered traffic shift 4) run chaos sim where us-west is flapped 5) run A/B eval for quality across variants

maya: minor: make sure logs include: steering_policy_id, decision_reason (probe, quota, cost), selected_variant, and last_probe_ts. that'll speed debugging. :+1:

sam: I'll draft the telemetry schema and a simple console mock. want to run an experiment in canary org next week.

alex: thanks — i'll open a short PR with the steering_policy proto, attach the canary plan and the ops checklist. we can iterate on weights and probe TTLs after results.

console-product: please include a short blurb for the rollout docs about "why probabilistic steering vs strict preference" — helps PMs explain to customers.

alex: will do. rolling this into next weeks planning slot.
